details:
Project Lunar Horizon is an interactive lunar landing-site planning tool developed to address the challenges of selecting suitable landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. Its purpose is to make complex astronomical and environmental information easier to explore, compare, and interpret.

Future lunar missions must consider several interconnected factors when selecting a landing site. Sunlight availability influences the potential for solar power generation, while the visibility of Earth determines opportunities for direct communication. These conditions vary depending on both the geographical location and the selected date and time.

How Project Lunar Horizon Works:

Project provides an accessible interface through which users can explore candidate lunar landing locations and evaluate environmental conditions over different dates.

The platform focuses on visualizing the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon. This allows users to understand illumination conditions, identify potential communication windows, and compare how these conditions change across candidate sites and time periods.

By presenting this information in a unified interface, the tool helps users examine multiple mission-planning considerations without having to navigate several complicated scientific resources independently.

Innovation and Creativity

The main innovation of Project lunar Horizon is its integration of astronomical visibility and landing-site comparison into one intuitive experience. Instead of treating sunlight and Earth visibility as unrelated factors, the project brings them together to support a more comprehensive evaluation process.

Its accessible design also makes scientific information easier to understand for students, educators, researchers, and people interested in lunar exploration.

Intended Impact

Project Lunar Horizon aims to support more informed lunar mission planning by making important environmental conditions easier to evaluate. It could help identify promising periods for surface operations, improve understanding of potential communication limitations, and support preliminary comparisons between candidate landing locations.

Ultimately, our vision is to contribute to safer, more efficient, and better-informed exploration of the lunar South Pole.
